goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same problem: Django querysets don't support negative slicing.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
goldens.reasoning: C2 flags the same missing null check on member before has_global_access is accessed.

goldens.comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
goldens.reasoning: C3 describes the same TypeError from calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime.
None of the candidates says the OptimizedCursorPaginator import refers to a class that doesn't exist.

candidates: Code allows negative offsets for queryset slicing but Django querysets do not support negative indexing - attempting queryset[-5:100] will fail
Missing null check for organization_context.member before accessing has_global_access - member can be None when user doesn't have membership, causing AttributeError for system auth requests

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key method calls math.floor() or math.ceil() directly on datetime fields, causing TypeError because datetime objects are not real numbers - needs to convert datetime to timestamp first like DateTimePaginator does
OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor doesn't convert cursor values to datetime for queries when the field is a datetime type
